# Review, pass 1 — secret-history-189-190 (§§189–190)

Method: units.json read word by word against packet.md, known-forms.json, novel-forms.json, the glossary, conventions.md and the published parts (01-06 as model; 177, 182-185, 186-188 and the glossary for house). No modern translation opened. Edits were made by script in place (`t`, `ln`, `p`, keys and `words` counts untouched).

Mechanical checks, all clean after the edits: every `t` equals the packet words of its run; 462 of 462 words consumed once, in order; one `words` entry per word; the `[bracket]` text of each word's morph glosses equals the packet's Ming gloss for that word (torluγ and torulmiši correctly carry none); `p: true` on the first unit of §189 and §190; double quotation marks balance (26).

Unit numbers below are 0-based positions in `sentences` (unit 0 = "Naiman-u Tajaṅ …", unit 38 = "Edeġer üges-tür …", first of §190).

## Changes

### Major
| unit · field | what was wrong | done |
|---|---|---|
| 23 · i, l, n, words | The word qor(i)-jar(i)-jan was left out of `i` altogether ("the render leaves it out"), and `l` carried it as "their-own quiver". The morph called jar(i) "a middle element, Ming 自的". The Ming 自的行 belongs to the reflexive -jan (as in qor(i)-jan, qonid(i)-jan); the glossary already has jar(i) as the instrumental -jar, and 151-153 has γažar(i)-jar the same way. Also "set him against them" had an unsupported "them" (Ming 反了 = "turned, rebelled"). | Split into qor + -(i) + -jar (instrumental) + -(i) + -jan. `l` "by-own-quiver", `i` "Those people, with their own quiver, frightened old Wang Qan … made him rebel, and caused his death." The note says the reflexive could point at Wang Qan and that what "by quiver" means is not stated. |
| 47 · i, l, n, words | elči-jer(i)-jen had the same wrong label ("middle element … I cannot say what -jer(i) is") and `i` made the envoy the object ("sent his own envoy"). The reading that fits the verb is the instrumental: word sent *through* his own envoy. | elči + -jer (instrumental, front-vowel -jar) + -(i) + -jen. `i` "sent word to Chinggis Qahan by his own envoy, named Juqunan, saying:". Note says it is uncertain (the Ming has no word for "by"). |
| 32, 33, 34 · i, n | Mixed persons. `i` said "we might bring … have them milk **our** own cows" but the chain ends in saγ̇aγ̇ulqun, a plural imperative ("you all", the draft's own label). A reflexive follows the subject of the imperative. | Chain read as advice to Tayang and his men: "Perhaps have their … brought … and perhaps have them milk **your** own cows and sheep. That is all." The note records "our own" as the other possibility. |
| about | Overreach: "the Önggüd leader" (the text only names Alaqush-Digit-Quri; Ming 人名), Tayang "looking east" (invented from dorona), and the council "argues that to lose the quiver is to lose all" (no such statement; Belgütei asks what use living is if one's quiver is taken by a follower). | Rewritten to what the units show. |

## Findings refused (checked and left)

- **torluγ / torulmiši left untranslated** (units 16, 19, 40). Kept. The Ming is blank, nothing in the grammar fixes a sense, and the house already does this for urubaṅ (182-185). The notes say so. I considered offering "born torluγ" as an epithet like "the Bold" and rejected it as invention.
- **ögčü left out of `i`** (unit 28). Kept; `l` keeps "giving" and the note says why. "We give" or "for us" would each add a claim the text does not make.
- **bütügei as "let them be"** (unit 31). Kept. The Ming here is 有者, the glossary's earlier entry reads 休 "do not"; the draft follows the Ming at each place and says so. For the glosser: the glossary's bütügei entry now needs an "also" for this use, and its prohibitive reading is itself only the Ming's 休.
- **ese bolba as a past negative** (unit 50). Labels are right (ese for the past, house); only the English changed.
- **-(γ̇)užai run** (units 51, 67-69). One label, "apprehensive ending", is consistent across all four and fits the Ming 恐 (unit 51) and 麽 (the others). I could not make it firmer; the notes say the reading is uncertain, and in 67-69 the English keeps the rhetorical question.
- **ülü-ü as negative + question particle** (units 64, 67-69). Left as uncertain; the Ming glosses plain 不 every time, so the question reading in unit 64 rests on sense only, as the note already says.
- **maqa as "perhaps"** (units 32, 34, 37). House (165-168) "perhaps (not)"; the Ming here is 莫不, which supports "perhaps … might we not". Kept.
- **tedeked / -ked, tede, "Kürbesü" as a name, Inancha-Bilge as Tayang's father, Inanča-Bilge's inner speech (units 14-16)**. The grammar and the "I had this Tayang born" content support the reading; the notes already call each uncertain. Kürbesü: the existing glossary key kürbesü is the conditional of kür-; the glosser will need an "also" for the name (Ming 人名).
- **ineġe- beside ine-** (units 7, 8). The Han (亦捏額罷) does write an extra syllable; kept as "form uncertain".
- **"omen" for the dogs' bark** (unit 12). Already flagged by the drafter as only 歹 "bad"; left.
- **torluγ and Qān min-u (unit 19) speaker**: who speaks units 17-19 is not marked. The draft assigns them to Kökse'ü-Sabraq inside the one print quote; Inancha-Bilge's words (14-16) end at keġeleġe, so I see no better assignment. Remains uncertain.
- **Segmentation** (71 units, §§ chips, p flags): acceptable; no unit needed splitting.

## Counts

Major 4 findings (touching 8 units plus `about`); Moderate 13 findings (about 45 unit-fields: quotation marks across 35 units, `l` name forms in 6, print marks in `l` in 24); Minor 18 findings. Refused: 12 items. Remaining uncertainty, stated in the notes: units 4 (chain subject), 8, 16/19/40 (torluγ, torulmiši), 23 (what "by quiver" means), 24 (aqun-u), 25 (quotation marks), 40 (the whole line), 47 (-jer), 51 and 67-69 (-užai), 64 (the question).
